types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Actor, Director, Writer. Examples: Brenda Fricker, Phil Belfield, Simon Harris, Christy Brown.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Person class directly matches the OIE_TYPE and examples.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

types.embedding_query_text: Award: A prize or honor given for achievement. Also called Prize, Honor, Recognition. Examples: Oscar, Academy Award, Academy Award for best supporting actress.

chosen_type.label: Award
chosen_type.definition: An honor or prize given for achievement in sports, typically for top performance in a competition.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a prize/honor; minting as a new entity under Thing.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: Film: A motion picture or movie. Also called Movie, Cinema, Production. Examples: My Left Foot, Home Alone 2, The Swallow, Veronica Guerin.

chosen_type.label: Movie
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Movie class aligns with the definition and examples of films.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: A character or part played by an actor. Also called Character, Part, Participation. Examples: Pigeon Lady.

chosen_type.label: PerformanceRole
chosen_type.justification: PerformanceRole specifically captures a character role in media, fitting 'Pigeon Lady' as a film character.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Play
candidates.comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.definition: A calendar date without time component, representing a temporal marker for events.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Date datatype matches the format and purpose of the examples (e.g., '2026-07-16').

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

types.embedding_query_text: Place: A location or geographic site. Also called Location, City, Country. Examples: Dublin, Central Park.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Place class fits the definition and examples like Dublin and Central Park.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

types.embedding_query_text: Position: An official post or title held by a person. Also called Role, Title, Post. Examples: Deputy Prime Minister.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationRole
chosen_type.justification: OrganizationRole captures official positions like 'Deputy Prime Minister' within a political structure.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: PostOffice
candidates.comment: A PostOffice is a GovernmentOffice providing postal services. Also called postal service branch, mail office. Examples: USPS Post Office, Royal Mail sorting office, a local post office branch, a general post office.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

types.embedding_query_text: Publication: A periodical or media outlet. Also called Newspaper, Magazine, Media. Examples: The Guardian, CBS News.

chosen_type.label: Newspaper
chosen_type.justification: Newspaper is a specific type of periodical matching 'The Guardian' and 'CBS News'.

candidates.label: Newspaper
candidates.comment: A Newspaper, as a Periodical, is a publication containing information about varied topics, often published daily. Also called daily paper, news publication, gazette. Examples: The Wall Street Journal, The Guardian, a local community newspaper. Distinct from Magazine, which is typically published weekly or monthly with a specific focus.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: PublicationEvent
candidates.comment: A PublicationEvent is an Event corresponding to the publication of a CreativeWork, regardless of its type or delivery medium. Also called release event, publishing event. Examples: the release of a new book, the broadcast of a TV show, the online publication of an article, the launch of a new album.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a common purpose. Also called Institution, Company, Agency. Examples: BBC.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Organization class directly applies to BBC as a structured entity.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

types.embedding_query_text: TVSeries: A series of television episodes with a continuous storyline. Also called Series, Show, Program. Examples: Casualty.

chosen_type.label: TVSeries
chosen_type.justification: TVSeries matches the definition of a television series with multiple episodes, as in 'Casualty'.

candidates.label: TVSeries
candidates.comment: A creative work series dedicated to television broadcast and associated online delivery, comprising multiple seasons and episodes. Also called television show, TV program, broadcast series. Examples: 'Game of Thrones', 'The Office', 'Stranger Things'.

candidates.label: TVEpisode
candidates.comment: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: PodcastSeries
candidates.comment: A PodcastSeries is a CreativeWorkSeries representing an episodic collection of digital audio or video files that users can download and listen to. Also called podcast, podcast show, audio series. Examples: "The Daily", "Serial", "Stuff You Should Know", "My Favorite Murder". Distinct from PodcastEpisode, which is a single installment of the series.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Book
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork consisting of a written or printed work, typically bound together and protected by a cover. Also called publication, volume, printed matter. Examples: "To Kill a Mockingbird", "The Lord of the Rings", "A textbook on physics". Distinct from BookSeries, which is a collection of books.

candidates.label: ShortStory
candidates.comment: A brief work of literature, typically written in narrative prose, focusing on a single plot or theme. Also called tale, novelette, short fiction, narrative. Examples: Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Tell-Tale Heart', O. Henry's 'The Gift of the Magi', a story from a literary magazine.

candidates.label: Chapter
candidates.comment: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.

candidates.label: BookSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries comprising a sequence of books published as a set or with a common theme. Also called book collection, literary series, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter series", "The Chronicles of Narnia", "A Song of Ice and Fire". Distinct from Book, which is a single volume.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

types.embedding_query_text: Character: A fictional persona in a narrative. Also called Figure, Persona, Protagonist. Examples: Kevin.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Person class includes fictional characters like 'Kevin' in the provided examples.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

candidates.label: TVEpisode
candidates.comment: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.

candidates.label: ComicStory
candidates.comment: Any indivisible, re-printable unit within a comic, encompassing interior narratives, covers, and backmatter. Also called comic narrative, comic segment, comic content. Examples: The main story in a comic book, a short backup story, a comic book cover, an editorial page. Distinct from ComicCoverArt, which is specifically the artwork on the cover.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation or sovereign state. Also called Nation, State, Region. Examples: Ireland.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Country class aligns with 'Ireland' as a sovereign state.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: OccupationalExperienceRequirements
candidates.comment: OccupationalExperienceRequirements is an intangible entity indicating employment-related experience requirements. Also called job experience, work experience criteria, professional background. Examples: '5 years of experience in software development', 'entry-level position', 'management experience required'. Distinct from EducationalOccupationalCredential, which specifies formal qualifications.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: EducationalOccupationalCredential

Also called degree, certificate, qualification, license. Examples: A Bachelor of Science degree, a Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, a high school diploma, a professional license.
